ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening under Law 10/2010; the SL must conduct a risk-based client due diligence (CDD) on its intended financial counterparties. For UBOs and shareholders: mandatory screening against the EU Financial Sanctions Database (EU Consolidated List), UK OFAC List, UN Consolidated List, Spanish Executive Committee of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering (SEBLAC) and the Agencia Tributaria’s List of Tax Havens and blacklists. Directors, officers, and UBOs must be screened for PEP status using a professional AML database (e.g., Refinitiv World-Check, LexisNexis, or Dow Jones). A written compliance policy and risk assessment must be adopted by the board prior to registration of the company.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry) – online name clearance platform: https://www.registradores.org/mercantil/denominaciones/
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: All corporate names must be exclusively in Spanish or in any of Spain’s co-official languages (Catalan, Galician, Basque) for registrable entities in those respective regions. Names in foreign alphabets must be romanized into standard Spanish characters without diacritical marks (except those native to co-official languages). The name must be unique and must not match an existing Spanish company name, nor be a near-identity (e.g., a name that is phonetically or graphically equivalent to an existing name). The name must be followed by 'S.L.' (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) or 'S.L.U.' when applicable.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, Banco, Caja, Financiera, Fintech, Inversión, Valores, Fondo de Inversión, Sociedad de Inversión, Negociado de Valores, Mercado de Valores, Clearing, Exchange, Bursátil, Algoritmia, Trading, Operador, Fiduciaria, Holding, Empresa de Servicios de Inversión

Words or expressions suggesting reference to the State or official public entities (e.g., 'Ibérica', 'Mercado', 'Banco de España', 'Ministerio', 'Instituto', 'Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores' – CNMV, 'Agencia Tributaria')
Names identical to companies appearing in the Official Gazette of the Mercantile Registry (BORME), including any names that are visually or phonetically misleadingly similar
Words contrary to laws, public order, morality, or that infringe third-party trademarks or copyright
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the name clearance (certificación negativa del Registro Mercantil Central) is rejected, the applicant must file a formal administrative appeal (recurso de alzada) with the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) within one (1) month from notification of rejection, pursuant to the Spanish Companies Act (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, article 408). Prior to filing the appeal, the applicant may file a new request using an alternative name, but the existing reservation of the rejected name is not extended. The appeal must include: (i) the denied name application number, (ii) a clear legal argument on the basis of prior-chosen name availability, (iii) any supporting documentation such as preliminary trademark search results. A decision is typically issued within one (1) to three (3) months. If the appeal fails, the applicant may file a further internal appeal (recurso potestativo no de reposición) before the same DGRN prior to judicial review.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are not permitted for an entity engaged in proprietary algorithmic high-frequency trading under the ISIC 6499 code scope. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Spain at a verifiable address where legal notices can be served and where its books, minutes, and corporate records are available. The registered office must be indicated in the deed of incorporation and registered with the Mercantile Registry. Though a virtual office can be used as a back-office or administrative address, a physical on-site location is required for the company to meet the 'effective management and control' test (centre of main interests) for Spanish corporate tax and regulatory purposes. The company must also hold a valid securities or investment services license from the CNMV (Comisión Nacional del Mercado de Valores) for market-making activities, and the physical presence criterion applies under MiFID II (Markets in Financial Instruments Directive) for conduct of business.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 75% within first two years of operation. The CNMV and Spanish financial intelligence unit (SEPBLAC) maintain a policy of unannounced on-site inspections for authorised investment firms. Probing under MiFID II requires documented records, personnel, and physical infrastructure. Given the sensitive algorithmic trading scope, an unannounced physical inspection is highly likely (estimated at 75% probability) within 24 months from license activation.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) - Tax Agency of Spain. Central filing portal: Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (https://sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es); commercial registry: Registro Mercantil (origin of incorporation); mandatory tax census: Censo de Empresarios, Profesionales y Retenedores (Forms 036/037).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Spanish SL: (1) execute formation deed before a Spanish notary and register the company at the Mercantile Registry; (2) apply for the provisional NIF (Número de Identificación Fiscal) via Form 036 before AEAT within the statutory post-incorporation window; (3) upon registry completion, obtain the definitive NIF (CIF-format letter plus seven digits and control character); (4) simultaneously enroll in the Spanish VAT census (Censo de Empresarios) using Form 036/037; (5) if the taxpayer is enrolled in the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) monthly VAT filing regime, additionally request SII technical credentials (software certificate/API certificate). Foreign shareholders require an NIF for non-resident entities; a non-resident entity acting through a Spanish establishment, permanent establishment or economic presence must appoint a tax representative (art. 45 Ley General Tributaria) and declare its opening via Form 030/036.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The ES_SL (Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada) is a resident corporation under art. 8 Ley 27/2014 (LIS) because it is incorporated in Spain, with registered office or effective place of management in Spain; it carries unlimited worldwide tax liability (art. 7 LIS). Not pass-through; the entity itself pays Impuesto sobre Sociedades at the standard 25% head-line rate (15% reduced rate only for newly created resident companies carrying out an economic activity subject to conditions of art. 29.3 LIS for the first two years). No application of territorial scope or tax-exempt zone: the Canary Islands ZEC special regime is not available for a mainland SL. Prior to first taxable period, a Board resolution and accounting/transfer-pricing policy should confirm the non-residence of counterparties and the non-application of permanent establishment risk.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in Spain. Relevant statutory opt-in/opt-out mechanisms for an algorithmically trading Spanish SL: (1) Optional group taxation (consolidación fiscal) under arts. 61-68 LIS, whereby a 75%-owned group may elect consolidated CIT, binding for at least three tax periods; (2) ETVE (entidad de tenencia de valores extranjeros) holding regime, being a corporate law (not form-based) election to apply the 95% participation-exemption on qualifying foreign dividends/capital gains (art. 21 LIS), subject to communicated use and substance; (3) VAT group election (Grupo de IVA, art. 84.Dos.2ª LIVA) for German/other EU affiliates lacking taxable person status in Spain, requiring prior AEAT authorization; (4) Hybrid-mismatch rules (art. 15 bis, 36, 37 LIS) contain no elective benefit - they automatically re-characterise or deny deductions; a taxpayer may, however, make binding annual tax adjustments to neutralize EU MDR/DAC6-reportable hybrid structures; (5) For an SL where ISIC 6499 proprietary trading is carried out, no transparency election is available; a pass-through structure would instead require formation of an AIE/UTE, which is not the case.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: IVA - Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (Spanish VAT). Governed by Ley 37/1992 de 28 de diciembre, Reglamento RD 1624/1992, as harmonized with EU Council Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: For established businesses in Spain there is no turnover threshold: VAT registration (via Form 036) is mandatory before the commencement of any economic activity. For non-established EU suppliers: EUR 10,000 intra-Community distance-sales threshold for supplies to Spanish consumers; above that threshold Spanish VAT registration is required. For non-EU suppliers: zero exemption threshold; any taxable supply of goods or services with the place of supply in Spain (e.g., electronically supplied services, trading services used in Spain) requires VAT registration, typically with a tax representative. For an algorithmic HFT SL, proprietary financial transactions (market-making, trading on own account) are VAT-exempt activities under art. 20.Uno.18º LIVA, therefore the entity will file periodic IVA returns from the zero/refund position, with no VAT charge on its trading margins; ancillary management fees rendered to clients (if any) would likewise be exempt financial intermediary services unless separately structured as taxable professional services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain does not operate a mandatory invoice pre-clearance/authorization model; nevertheless, a real-time fiscal-return obligation applies under the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) for taxpayers exceeding EUR 6,010,121.04 annual billing threshold or enrolled in the REDEME monthly-refund regime. SII requires the detail of issued and received invoices (including modifications and ceased invoices) to be transmitted via AEAT web services/API in XSD format within 4 calendar days of the relevant record event (8 days in specific transitional arrangements), effectively constituting electronically enforced real-time fiscal clearance. In addition, Ley 18/2022 'Crea y Crece' mandates universal B2B electronic invoicing in Spain, and royal decree 1007/2023 establishes the VERIFACTU technical standard, which requires billing software to generate a sequential hash-chain record of each invoice with cryptographic integrity and to make the invoice data accessible to AEAT upon request; software producers must be declared and comply from stages in 2025/2026. No physical tax stamp or QR code is currently required for invoices. For the HFT SL, automatic trading files and confirmation statements must be reconciled to the SII/VERIFACTU invoice book should it exceed the SII threshold; even where all revenue is VAT-exempt, the entity remains obligated to maintain electronic books of invoices received and transactions under art. 63 and 65 RD 1624/1992.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: (1) Goods: 0% zero-rating (in practice exemption with credit) applies under art. 21 LIVA where tangible goods are dispatched or transported by the seller, by the purchaser not established in Spanish tax territory, or on behalf of either, directly to a destination outside the EU from Spanish territory, provided the exporter substantiates the movement of goods, retains the original or certified export documents, and, where required, the goods leave the EU within 3 months of dispatch (extensions possible on due justification). (2) Services: international services are treated as not subject to Spanish VAT (outside of scope), not 'zero-rated', when supplied to a business customer established outside the EU (art. 69.1 LIVA); ancillary services linked to exported goods (e.g., temporary storage, freight, insurance for goods destined to non-EU countries) may be exempt under art. 22 LIVA. Claim prerequisites in both cases include the vendor's retention of the customer's identity and fiscal residence certificate (IVA/CIF/VAT number or non-EU tax certificate), contractual documentation, invoices identifying the non-EU nature of the service, and journal evidence that the service was not consumed in Spain. For a proprietary HFT SL, if the only activity is on-exchange algorithmic trading, the income does not constitute exportable services; however, any sub-licensing or trade-execution services supplied to non-EU counterparties must be supported by residence certificates and records of the customer's establishment outside Spain to justify non-subjection in Spain and, where input tax was borne, recovery under the pro-rata rules of art. 104-112 LIVA.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration - Documento Único Administrativo (DUA/SAD) accepted by the Spanish customs authority, with EORI number of the exporter

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR / CIM consignment note evidencing the physical departure of the goods to a non-EU destination, or, for services, a contractual agreement, professional invoice, proof of customer establishment (certificate of tax residence or equivalent) and technical/transaction records demonstrating performance

Inward Remittance Certificate - Spanish banking evidence of the foreign currency receipt, typically SWIFT/MT103 or bank credit statement showing conversion and entry of funds into the Spanish account, attested where requested by the Banco de España
Commercial invoice, packing list, and, if applicable, Intrastat/ex-customs transit documentation (T1/T2) or certificates of origin
Any transport company/Customs agent certificate of release of the goods outside the EU and, for volumes subject to SII, the corresponding invoice event files declared in the AEAT web services
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: AEAT routinely scrutinizes export exemption claims under art. 21 LIVA, especially in algorithmic trading ecosystems where cross-border flows are high-speed and documentation may be tokenized or automated. If the export or international-service conditions, the customs documentation, or the 180-day FX collection trail are not fully substantiated, the tax office recharacterizes the revenue as taxable domestic supply, assessing: (i) the undeclared IVA, (ii) late payment interest (interés de demora) under art. 26 LGT, (iii) penalties under arts. 191-195 Ley 58/2003: 15% of the unduly settled amount where the omission is not significant; 50% where there is concealment; and 100%-150% in cases of 'concurso de fraude' (fraudulent collusion in the use of false invoices or artificial transactions). Specific clawback rules under arts. 193-194 LGT allow recovery of undue refunds together with penalty equal to 50% of the amount improperly refunded. The corporate income tax anger for EUR 120,000+ declarations occasions criminal liability under art. 305 Código Penal (imprisonment of one to five years) against the legal representative/tax professional; the corporate SL itself may face the corporate penalty art. 310 bis. The assessment period is 4 years, which is interrupted by verifiable fraud audits; export remission of prescription is excluded where records have been falsified. In addition, an HS code misdeclaration or false EORI/representative statement entails customs sanctions under Código Aduanero together with suspension of the exporter's authorization. For an HFT SL, audit risk is mitigated only by maintaining an immutable chronological tax data lake containing order/trade timestamps, execution venue statements, bank credits, reconciliation to SII/VERIFACTU invoice books, and the underlying ISIC 6499/NAICS 523130 business documentation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) as central bank and Eurosystem member, acting in coordination with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business) for foreign-exchange statistical and anti-money-laundering oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain, as a Eurozone Member State, has full convertibility of the euro under the EU Treaty freedoms (TFEU Article 63) for current and capital transactions. No Spanish exchange-control or currency-approval regime restricts profit remittance; however, the Beneficial-Ownership Directive, EU sanctions regimes, and anti-money-laundering legislation may cause documentary or prudential delays. Outbound dividend, interest, and fee remittances to non-residents are subject to non-resident income tax withholding (generally 19%) unless reduced under an applicable tax treaty.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Spain imposes no mandatory export-proceeds surrender or forced conversion into euros. Export receipts may remain in foreign currency in authorised bank accounts. A balance-of-payments statistical declaration to Banco de España is required for single transactions equal to or exceeding €50,000 within 30 days after settlement. Commercial invoicing and payment terms are freely negotiated and no statutory repatriation deadline is prescribed beyond the contractual term, subject to EU/UN sanctions compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium – EU/EEA-licensed electronic money institutions (EMIs) passporting into Spain may open euro and multicurrency accounts for treasury settlement, but they are not credit institutions, lack deposit-guarantee coverage, cannot directly hold funds at Banco de España, and may not support the ultra-low-latency clearing rails and Fedwire-compatible settlement required for algorithmic high-frequency trading. EMI viability is legally constrained under the Spanish regime (Royal Decree 19/2018 on payment services and electronic money) and Bank of Spain registration; only low-complexity, non-critical treasury flows are advisable.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical or hybrid video interview with the beneficial owners and at least one director and the compliance officer is normally mandatory when opening a corporate account for an algorithmic trading entity. Spanish banks generally require in-branch appearance of the legal representative with notarised and apostilled corporate documentation; remote onboarding may be accepted for lower-risk structures under the Bank of Spain's SEPBLAC-approved remote KYC guidelines, but is rarely granted for proprietary trading firms without a MiFID II licence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-Spanish beneficial ownership originating in jurisdictions with perceived strategic or tax secrecy gaps and a capital-injection history with frequent wire volumes.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled share register and UBO certificates with national ID/passport copies, tax-residence certificates from all jurisdictions, notarial source-of-wealth affidavit, bank reference letters covering a 12-month transaction history, audited financial statements of each parent entity, and a board-approved corporate treasury memo describing the funding and trading rationale.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual cross-border wire activity involving rapid FX conversions and settlements through third-party clearing systems (Fedwire, Direct Exchange Clearing) without a clear market-making explanation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed MiFID II / CNMV regulatory licence (or exemption letter), the company's HFT and market-making strategy documentation, counterparty due-diligence file, algorithm white paper and risk-control description, transaction-monitoring system configuration, and a list of authorised traders with compliance attestations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High trade-netting volumes and low duration between inbound and outbound fund movements, causing suspicion of money laundering via over-the-counter derivative contracts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed recurring FX forward/swaps master agreements (ISDA/CSA), daily P&L reconciliation with confirmations, fund-flow reconciliation report with SWIFT tags, licensing/registration under EMIR with LEI, and an external auditor's certification of the AML/CFT risk assessment and internal control framework.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders shall send capital via SWIFT MT103 with the purpose code either 'INVC' (investment capital) or the customer-specific Bank of Spain statistical code for direct investment (FDI). The transfer must reference the Spanish company's Tax ID (NIF) and the notarised 'escritura' of the capital increase; for investments above €3,000,000, the post-investment declaration to the Foreign Investment Registry (Registro de Inversiones Exteriores) must be filed within one month, and the receiving bank may require a copy of the stamped filing. Funds are then held in a segregated account in euros or foreign currency, subject to standard source-of-funds verification.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For euro disbursements, use TARGET2 or SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst). For non-euro trade settlements, issue SWIFT MT103 with an end-to-end reference and use the correspondent banking network; USD settlements must reach a Fedwire member bank using the recipient's Fedwire routing number, with payment instructions authenticated via SWIFT FIN or a tested telex. Commercial letters of credit may be advised through the corporate bank's trade finance desk for documentary trade, subject to UCP 600 and full EU sanctions screening.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (EUR/USD and EUR/GBP, custom tenors)
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on emerging-market non-convertible currencies
Cross-Currency Swaps (CCS or XCCY) for long-term treasury alignment
FX Swaps (spot against forward) for liquidity and rollover management
Vanilla FX Options (calls and puts) and foreign-exchange futures on regulated venues, in each case under EMIR clearing and MiFID II execution rules

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil (Commercial Registry) of the province of the company's registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual accounts must be approved by the shareholders' general meeting within six months of the fiscal year-end and filed with the Registry within one month of approval. For a calendar-year entity, the final legal deadline is 31 July of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late deposit triggers administrative fines under the Mercantile Registry sanctioning procedure (typically EUR 600–6,000 per year of delay); the company cannot file other documents in any commercial registry until outstanding accounts are deposited; after two consecutive years of non-deposit, administrative strike-off proceedings (cierre registral) may be initiated and directors may be personally liable.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return – Sociedad Limitada (Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed within 25 calendar days after the 6-month post-close period. For a taxable year ending 31 December, the return is due by 25 July of the following tax year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing without prior AEAT notice incurs an automatic surcharge of 5% of the tax due, rising to 10%, 15%, or 20% based on the delay, plus late-payment interest; filing after a formal tax administration notice raises the surcharge to 50%–150% of the assessed liability; total penalties capped at the amount of tax, and prolonged non-filing can lead to criminal tax charges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due simultaneously with the Modelo 200 corporate tax return; for a calendar-year entity, by 25 July. Mandatory only if related-party transactions in the tax year exceed EUR 250,000 or transactions with tax havens exceed EUR 100,000.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late, incomplete, or unintentionally inaccurate filing is penalized under Article 198 of the General Tax Law with EUR 200–5,000 for late presentation; materially incorrect data can draw additional penalties of EUR 1,000 per data item or group of data, with minimum penalties of EUR 10,000 for intentional wrongdoing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada is obliged to have its individual annual accounts audited by a registered auditor (ROAC) if, for two consecutive years, it satisfies at least two of the following three conditions: total balance-sheet assets exceed EUR 2,850,000; annual net revenue exceeds EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees exceeds 50. Companies belonging to a group that produces consolidated IFRS accounts are also compulsorily audited, and an audit must be appointed at the request of shareholders holding at least 5% of the share capital.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts are prepared under Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad) issued by the ICAC, while consolidated accounts of a Spanish-parent group comply with EU-adopted IFRS (NIIF). The accounts comprise the balance sheet, profit and loss account, changes in equity statement, cash-flow statement, and notes to the financial statements, and they must give a true and fair view of the entity's assets, equity, and results.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Spain does not establish a separate annual UBO confirmation form. Under Law 10/2010 and the Spanish implementing regulations, the SL must keep an up-to-date internal register of ultimate beneficial owners and, where a share transfer occurs, record the transfer in the share registry, execute a public deed before a notary, and inscribe the change with the Mercantile Registry. The annual shareholders' meeting approving the annual accounts, the deposit of those accounts, and the current data filed with the Registro Mercantil collectively constitute the periodic confirmation of the ownership structure for the calendar year.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 – USD 2,500 per annum for a registered office/agent service in Madrid or Barcelona, including notarial and registry assistance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 5,000 – USD 20,000 per annum for a compulsory audit of a mid-size SL engaged in proprietary algorithmic trading; scope and complexity of intercompany transactions may increase the fee

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax rate for a Spanish Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada. Newly incorporated entities generally qualify for a 15% rate in the first tax period in which they obtain a taxable profit and the immediately following tax period, subject to statutory exclusions and anti-abuse rules.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Tax losses may be carried forward indefinitely, subject to taxable-base utilization limits generally ranging from 25% to 70% depending on prior-year net turnover, together with a EUR 1 million minimum utilization threshold. Qualifying research and development, technological innovation, patent-box, investment, employment, and other statutory tax credits may reduce the effective rate. The 15% newly created-entity rate is unavailable where the entity forms part of a pre-existing business restructuring or is controlled by a pre-existing related business in circumstances covered by the Corporate Income Tax Law.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200, annual Corporate Income Tax return, filed electronically through the Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) electronic headquarters. Modelo 202 is used for mandatory advance Corporate Income Tax payments. Modelo 222 applies only to tax-consolidated groups.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, with advance payments generally in April, October, and December.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Modelo 200 is due within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual filing window is 1 to 25 July of the following year. Modelo 202 is generally due during the first 20 calendar days of April, October, and December; the October and December deadlines may extend to the first 15 calendar days when electronic direct debit is used.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, Spanish tax identification number (NIF), registered address, legal form, tax period, activity codes, turnover indicators, and electronic filing status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident shareholder or director is not itself reported as the taxpayer. The Spanish SL files using its own NIF and must identify foreign related parties, ultimate beneficial owners, and permanent-establishment information where applicable.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting assets, liabilities, equity, revenue, expenses, financial income, financial expenses, trading gains and losses, and tax-accounting adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Record the Spanish entity's worldwide accounting result. Do not exclude foreign-source income merely because shareholders, counterparties, clearing brokers, or service providers are non-resident.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary differences between Spanish GAAP or IFRS accounting profit and the taxable base, including non-deductible expenses, provisions, depreciation differences, valuation adjustments, exempt income, and tax incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply Spanish deductibility, documentation, related-party, interest-limitation, anti-hybrid, and anti-abuse rules. Foreign tax treatment does not determine Spanish deductibility.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Realized and unrealized valuation movements, derivatives income, exchange gains and losses, financing costs, market-data costs, colocation, telecommunications, software, and execution expenses, classified consistently with applicable accounting standards and tax rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain trade-level records, valuation policies, broker statements, exchange confirmations, and evidence of business purpose. Separate proprietary trading income from client, agency, brokerage, or investment-management income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure and reconciliation of transactions with group companies, directors, shareholders, foreign affiliates, financing entities, technology providers, and centralized treasury or service companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify non-resident related parties by jurisdiction and tax identification number where required. Reconcile the return to transfer-pricing documentation and statutory related-party disclosures.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Opening losses, losses utilized, losses generated, and closing balances, subject to statutory utilization limits and anti-loss-trafficking rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Maintain proof of losses and ownership continuity. Acquired or materially transformed loss companies may be denied use of historic losses under anti-abuse provisions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research and development, technological innovation, double-taxation, employment, investment, patent-box, and other available credits, with supporting calculations and carryforward balances.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign parent cannot automatically claim Spanish credits. Eligibility depends on expenditure, Spanish nexus, certification, documentation, and statutory substantiation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Taxable base and Corporate Income Tax liability
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Adjusted taxable base, applicable rate, gross liability, credits, advance payments, withholding taxes, final balance, and amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the standard 25% rate unless the entity demonstrably qualifies for a specific reduced rate or regime. Reconcile the final liability with Modelo 202 payments and Spanish withholding certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Payment, bank account, and electronic signature
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Payment reference, direct debit or electronic payment details, refund account, authorized filer, and electronic signature.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign directors may authorize a Spanish tax representative or electronic filing agent. The company remains responsible for the accuracy and timely filing of the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payment based either on the prior-period assessment or on the current-period taxable base method, subject to statutory election, turnover thresholds, and minimum payment rules for large taxpayers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the current-base method only after confirming the applicable election and statutory conditions. Reconcile trading volatility, derivatives valuation, and year-to-date accounting data before each payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Modelo 123 reports quarterly withholding on dividends, interest, royalties, and other income subject to Spanish withholding. Modelo 193 provides the annual informational summary.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Obtain valid residency certificates and beneficial-owner evidence before applying treaty or EU exemptions. Report payments even where the withholding rate is reduced to zero, when required by the applicable form rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without tax payable generally attracts a fixed penalty under the General Tax Law, commonly EUR 200, normally reduced by 50% for voluntary filing without prior administrative notice. Where tax is payable and filing is voluntary, a surcharge generally applies at 1% plus 1% for each complete month of delay during the first 12 months, and 15% thereafter, with late-payment interest generally applying after 12 months. Failure to make advance payments may generate the unpaid amount, late-payment interest, and penalties for tax-base understatement or culpable non-compliance. Inaccurate or fraudulent returns may attract penalties of 50% to 150% of the improperly avoided amount, subject to the statutory classification and aggravating factors.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 232, related-party and tax-haven transaction information return, filed electronically through the AEAT electronic headquarters when the statutory transaction thresholds are met.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally due during the month following the ten-month period after the end of the tax period. For a calendar-year taxpayer, the usual deadline is 30 November.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Type of transaction, related-party counterparty, jurisdiction, amount, and transfer-pricing method.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include non-resident related parties and identify transactions by category, including financing, services, technology, licensing, and intra-group cost allocations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Aggregate transaction amounts and category-specific thresholds determining whether reporting is mandatory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Assess thresholds by related party and transaction type using Spanish tax-law definitions, not only accounting materiality.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Transactions and holdings involving jurisdictions listed under Spain's non-cooperative jurisdiction rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply enhanced review, beneficial-ownership verification, substance analysis, and documentation where any counterparty, payment route, or ownership chain involves a listed jurisdiction.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file or filing incorrect information may result in fixed penalties under the General Tax Law, commonly calculated by data or omitted-data items, subject to statutory minimums and maximums. Deliberate concealment, false records, or use of sham counterparties may also trigger tax-evasion, accounting, money-laundering, or criminal liability.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% Spanish withholding on dividends and other income from participation in equity paid to non-residents, subject to domestic exemptions, EU rules, tax treaties, and anti-abuse requirements.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Before payment, obtain a current certificate of tax residence issued by the recipient's competent foreign tax authority, verify beneficial ownership, legal entitlement, minimum holding and holding-period conditions, limitation-on-benefits or principal-purpose requirements where applicable, and retain corporate resolutions, payment records, ownership evidence, and substance documentation. Apply the treaty rate only where the payer can substantiate entitlement. If evidence is unavailable at payment, withhold at the domestic rate and pursue the applicable refund procedure through the AEAT. Dividends paid to a qualifying EU or European Economic Area parent may be exempt under the Spanish implementation of the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, generally requiring at least a 10% direct holding, the applicable minimum holding period or commitment, subject-to-tax conditions, and anti-abuse compliance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The domestic Spanish withholding rate is generally 24% on interest and royalties paid to non-residents, subject to special rules and exemptions. Qualifying interest and royalty payments between associated companies in different EU Member States may be exempt under the EU Interest and Royalties Directive as implemented in Spain, commonly requiring a qualifying legal form, subject-to-tax status, minimum 25% direct or indirect relationship, minimum holding period or commitment, and beneficial ownership. Spanish tax treaties commonly reduce interest and royalty withholding to rates ranging from 0% to 10%, but the exact rate depends on the recipient's residence jurisdiction, treaty text, beneficial ownership, and anti-abuse provisions. Payments to related parties in non-cooperative jurisdictions require enhanced analysis and may be denied relief.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Spain generally requires local transfer-pricing documentation for controlled transactions unless a statutory exception applies. A principal quantitative exception applies where the aggregate value of transactions with the same related person or entity does not exceed EUR 250,000 at arm's length value during the tax period, subject to exclusions and transaction-type rules. A master file is generally required for Spanish entities belonging to a group with consolidated net turnover of at least EUR 45 million, subject to statutory exemptions. The EUR 250,000 threshold is not a universal safe harbor for transactions involving certain real-estate, intangible-asset, or non-cooperative-jurisdiction categories.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Other OECD-consistent methods where the prescribed methods cannot reliably be applied
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain has no separate standalone Economic Substance Regulations equivalent to the UAE ESR regime. Substance is nevertheless material under Spanish transfer-pricing, beneficial-ownership, principal-purpose, anti-abuse, controlled foreign company, hybrid-mismatch, interest-limitation, withholding-tax, and general anti-avoidance rules. The SL should maintain Spanish decision-making, qualified personnel, premises or operational infrastructure appropriate to its functions, risk controls, trading authority, technology oversight, independent accounting, bank and exchange records, and evidence that algorithms, capital, market risk, and management functions are genuinely located where represented. A purely conduit or artificial entity may lose treaty, EU-directive, deduction, or participation-exemption benefits and may face recharacterization.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concealing proprietary trading profits, fabricating expenses, using false invoices, omitting foreign accounts or related parties, manipulating valuation records, or knowingly filing materially false Corporate Income Tax or withholding returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalties may generally range from 50% to 150% of the improperly avoided tax, depending on the seriousness, concealment, and recurrence. Serious tax fraud exceeding the applicable Criminal Code threshold may lead to imprisonment and criminal fines; aggravated tax fraud involving organized structures or particularly large amounts carries higher sanctions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers who participate, authorize, or negligently facilitate the conduct may face criminal liability, civil liability for tax debt and restitution, administrative disqualification, and seizure of assets. A travel ban is not automatic and requires a competent authority or court order. The corporate veil is not pierced merely because a company has tax debt.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificially shifting trading profits through non-arm's-length financing, technology, data, execution, management, or licensing charges, or maintaining documentation that does not match actual functions, assets, and risks.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may make a primary adjustment, impose compensating or secondary consequences, deny deductions, assess withholding tax, and impose transfer-pricing documentation or valuation penalties. Specific documentation penalties may apply per omitted, inaccurate, or incomplete data, subject to statutory limits; general tax penalties may also apply where tax is underpaid.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may incur civil liability to the company and, where intentional participation or gross negligence is proven, personal administrative or criminal exposure. Mere failure to achieve a particular profit margin does not establish liability.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying dividends, interest, or royalties without withholding, applying treaty relief without a valid residence certificate or beneficial-owner basis, routing payments through conduit entities, or backdating ownership and documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The company may owe the unpaid withholding, late-payment interest, and penalties generally calculated as a percentage of the unpaid amount, potentially reaching 150% in aggravated cases. Treaty or EU exemptions may be denied and the recipient may face refund denial or reassessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve unsupported zero withholding or sham conduit arrangements may face civil restitution, administrative sanctions, and criminal exposure where fraud is involved. Travel restrictions require a specific legal or judicial order and are not an automatic tax consequence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money laundering, terrorist financing, and beneficial-ownership concealment
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using undisclosed beneficial owners, unexplained third-party funding, nominee arrangements, cash or crypto settlement designed to obscure proceeds, false source-of-funds evidence, or transfers involving sanctioned or non-cooperative jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Spanish anti-money-laundering breaches may attract substantial administrative fines, public or private reprimands, license or authorization consequences, and director disqualification. Money laundering and terrorist-financing conduct may constitute crimes punishable by imprisonment and criminal fines, with aggravated sanctions for professional, organized, or repeated conduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and controlling persons may be personally liable where they order, facilitate, knowingly tolerate, or seriously neglect legally required controls. Courts may impose asset freezing, confiscation, management disqualification, or travel restrictions where legally justified.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unauthorized investment services and market abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Providing execution, dealing, market making for clients, portfolio management, investment advice, or venue access without required authorization; deploying algorithms without required controls; spoofing, layering, quote stuffing, front-running, insider dealing, or market manipulation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CNMV and other competent authorities may impose significant administrative fines, cease-and-desist orders, authorization restrictions, suspension, prohibition of activity, and publication of sanctions. Market-abuse and unauthorized-investment-services conduct may also constitute criminal offences involving imprisonment and fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and algorithm owners may be personally liable for intentional or negligent failures in governance, testing, kill-switches, surveillance, recordkeeping, and escalation. Corporate limited liability does not protect individuals who personally commit or direct the violation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Destroying order or trade logs, altering timestamps, maintaining inadequate books, concealing related-party transactions, using unapproved production code, or failing to preserve records required by tax, securities, market-abuse, and accounting rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Consequences may include tax penalties, accounting sanctions, regulatory fines, evidentiary adverse inferences, rejection of deductions, audit reassessments, and criminal liability for falsification or obstruction. Severe control failures may cause suspension of trading or regulatory authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face company-law liability for failure of diligence, civil damages, disqualification, and criminal exposure where records were falsified or intentionally destroyed. Insolvency-related liability may arise if the failure contributed to creditor prejudice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Continuing leveraged trading while insolvent, preferring related-party creditors, extracting dividends despite impaired capital or creditor prejudice, transferring algorithms or cash below value, or delaying required insolvency action.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transactions may be rescinded, assets recovered, and directors disqualified. The insolvency estate may seek damages, repayment of unlawful distributions, and liability for the insolvency deficit where the insolvency is classified as culpable. Fraudulent asset transfers may also constitute criminal offences.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil restitution, liability for the insolvency deficit, disqualification from administration of third-party assets, and imprisonment for fraudulent insolvency or asset concealment. Travel bans are exceptional and depend on court orders; they are not an automatic consequence of ordinary insolvency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and artificial substance arrangement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a Spanish SL with no genuine personnel, governance, risk control, capital, technology oversight, or decision-making while booking trading profits solely to obtain treaty, EU, financing, or tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The AEAT may apply general anti-avoidance or conflict-in-application rules, deny exemptions and deductions, recharacterize transactions, assess tax and interest, impose penalties where culpability is established, and disregard unsupported beneficial-owner or residence claims.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face civil and administrative liability for deliberate abuse, and criminal liability if the arrangement includes tax fraud, false accounting, money laundering, or document falsification. Limited liability remains available for genuine corporate debts and is not automatically defeated by low substance alone.
